newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Consumer price comeback.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Consumer price comeback.

text.p: The U.S. credit market is bracing for Wednesday's consumer price index to show decent gains for the month of September after a meager advance in August, analysts said.

Economists surveyed by Reuters are calling for gains of 0.3 percent in both the overall and core consumer price readings for September following 0.1 percent advances in both readings in the prior month.
"The market would probably read those numbers as evidence that inflation has not become a problem yet," said Dan Seto, senior economist at Nikko Securities Co International Inc.
A bounceback in apparel and strength in the transportation sector, resulting from a reintroduction of an airline excise tax, probably boosted consumer prices in September, economists said.
But barring a gain significantly higher than consensus, the market could wait until October consumer price figures before worrying about inflation.
Economists said that the recently enacted minimum wage rise should begin filtering through begining with the October numbers.

Alan Levenson, money market economist at UBS Securities Inc, is forecasting a 0.2 percent overall consumer price gain and a 0.3 percent jump in the core reading, which would keep the year-over-year inflation reading where it was in the previous month.
"It seems to me there is more likely to be a strong positive reaction to a weak number than a negative reaction to a strong number," said Levenson.

In addition to the September CPI report, September real earnings and the October homebuilders survey will also be released on Wednesday, although the latter reports are unlikely to have a major market impact.

The benchmark 6.75 percent 30-year bond was up 1/32 at 98-26/32 to yield 6.84 percent in late trading on Tuesday. The federal funds rate is expected to open in line with the Fed's target at 5-1/4 percent on Wednesday.
